name: Love Style Test
tagline: Find out how you most like to give and receive love.
intro: People express and recognise love in different ways: through words, shared time, gifts, practical help or physical closeness. This test shows which of these five love styles speak to you most, and which matter less. Answer with your closest relationships in mind, romantic or otherwise. It takes about five minutes and can help you understand yourself and the people you love.
seoTitle: Love Style Test: How do you give and receive love?
seoDescription: Words, time, gifts, help or touch? Take this free 5-minute love style test and discover how you prefer to give and receive affection.

words.name: Words of appreciation
words.short: How much spoken and written appreciation makes you feel loved.
words.low: Kind words are pleasant for you, but they are not what makes you feel truly loved. You probably trust actions, presence or touch more than compliments. Keep in mind that people close to you may rely on words much more than you do. Saying a short, specific thank you or telling someone what you admire about them costs little and can mean a lot to them. Try to make it a small daily habit, even if it does not come naturally.
words.mid: Words of appreciation matter to you, but they are one part of a wider picture. A sincere compliment or encouraging message can brighten your day, yet you also feel loved through other gestures. This balance makes you flexible. One tip: notice which kind of words move you most, such as praise, gratitude or encouragement, and let your partner or friends know. Being specific about what you would like to hear makes it easier for others to give it.
words.high: Words are one of the most powerful ways for you to feel loved. Compliments, thanks, encouragement and messages of affection stay with you, while criticism or silence can hurt deeply. You probably also express your own love generously in words. Let the people close to you know how much their words matter, since they may not realise it. At the same time, try to recognise love expressed in other ways, so you do not miss affection that comes without words.

time.name: Quality time
time.short: How much undivided attention and shared moments make you feel loved.
time.low: Spending lots of time together is not the main way you feel loved. You may be comfortable with independence and value other signals more, such as help, gifts or kind words. That is perfectly fine. Just remember that for many people, especially partners, time together is essential. Planning a regular moment without distractions, even a short walk or a shared meal, can strengthen your relationships without asking much of you.
time.mid: You enjoy shared moments and attention, but you do not need constant togetherness to feel loved. Time together is important to you alongside other ways of connecting. A useful tip is to protect a few quality moments each week rather than aiming for large amounts of time. Put phones away, choose an activity you both enjoy and notice how it affects your sense of closeness. Small rituals often matter more than grand plans.
time.high: Undivided attention is one of the clearest signs of love for you. Long conversations, shared activities and simply being together make you feel valued, while distraction or cancelled plans can feel like rejection. Tell the people close to you that their presence matters more than gifts or grand gestures. Agree on regular, protected time together. At the same time, try not to measure love only in hours, since busy periods do not always mean someone cares less.

gifts.name: Thoughtful gifts
gifts.short: How much meaningful presents and tokens of attention make you feel loved.
gifts.low: Gifts are not a major part of how you experience love. You may find them nice but unnecessary, or even feel uneasy about receiving them. Other forms of care probably say more to you. Keep in mind that for some people a small present is a deeply meaningful sign of attention. Remembering important dates or bringing back a small token now and then can make a big difference to someone who values gifts more than you do.
gifts.mid: You appreciate a thoughtful present, especially when it shows that someone thought of you, but gifts are not the only way you feel loved. The meaning behind a gift probably matters more to you than its price. One tip: share small wishes or ideas with the people close to you, so they know what would delight you. In return, notice what others care about and surprise them occasionally with a simple, personal gesture.
gifts.high: For you, gifts are visible symbols of love and attention. A thoughtful present, however small, shows that someone thought of you, and you probably treasure the things you receive. Forgotten occasions can hurt. This has little to do with money and everything to do with meaning. Let the people close to you know that small, personal tokens matter to you. Also try to recognise love shown in other ways, so a missing gift does not overshadow other signs of care.

service.name: Practical help
service.short: How much practical help and support make you feel loved.
service.low: Practical help is not the main way you feel loved. You may prefer to do things yourself or value words, time or closeness more. That is perfectly valid. Still, for many people, help with everyday tasks is a strong sign of care. Offering to take over a chore, run an errand or solve a small problem can mean much more to them than you might expect. Ask the people around you which kind of help they would appreciate.
service.mid: You appreciate help and practical support, but it is one of several ways you feel cared for. When someone lightens your load, you notice and value it, yet you also feel loved through other gestures. A useful tip is to be clear about what kind of help you would welcome, rather than hoping others will guess. Equally, ask the people close to you which tasks they would love some help with.
service.high: For you, actions really do speak louder than words. When someone takes something off your plate, fixes a problem or makes your day easier, you feel deeply cared for. Broken promises or being left to do everything alone can hurt. Let the people close to you know which kinds of help mean the most, since they may not realise it. Also watch that you do not overload yourself by constantly helping others while hesitating to ask for help yourself.

touch.name: Physical closeness
touch.short: How much hugs, touch and physical presence make you feel loved.
touch.low: Physical affection is not a central way for you to feel loved, and you may value personal space. That is completely fine, and your boundaries deserve respect. Keep in mind that for some people a hug or a hand to hold is essential to feeling connected. Talk openly about what kind of touch you are comfortable with, so others do not mistake your preference for a lack of affection, and look for other ways to show warmth.
touch.mid: You enjoy physical affection in the right moments, but it is not the only way you feel connected. A hug or a hand on your shoulder can comfort you, while words, time or help also matter to you. One tip: notice when touch helps you most, for example during stress or after time apart, and let people close to you know. Clear signals help others offer closeness when you need it.
touch.high: Physical closeness is one of the strongest ways for you to feel loved. Hugs, holding hands or simply sitting close make you feel safe and connected, while a lack of touch can make you feel distant or lonely. Let the people close to you know how much this matters to you. Remember that others may have different comfort levels, so ask and respect boundaries. Small, frequent gestures often work better than waiting for big moments.

summary: Everyone gives and receives love in several ways, but most people have one or two that matter most. Your highest score shows your main love style; lower scores show what matters less to you, not what you lack. Sharing your results with the people you love can help you understand each other better.
